entries.title: Dragon Age Journeys

emulation.emulator: Flash preservation environment if legally archived

primary.why: Dragon Age Journeys is documented as a Flash-based browser tie-in to Origins. Only the first chapter was released, and the planned later chapters were cancelled, so the original browser release is the preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: No normal modern browser route is guaranteed because it required Flash. Preserve only verified archival builds/captures and do not claim the cancelled chapters exist.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release route; Flash dependency is the practical blocker.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official sourced platform.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only Chapter 1 was released; unreleased chapters are not counted as playable content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Flash-based and not normally playable in modern browsers.

entries.title: Dragon Age Legends

primary.why: Dragon Age Legends was a Flash social game for Facebook, Google+, and web browser. Its servers were shut down in 2012, but a free standalone Adobe AIR version released after shutdown, making that the best preservation route for the core game.
primary.how_to_play: Use the post-shutdown standalone build only if it can be legally and safely obtained. Treat social-platform features as retired.

secondary.exclusive_content: Dragon Age Legends: Remix 01, a modified hack-and-slash browser version.
secondary.what_to_play: Play/document the Remix 01 variant separately if a verified archival route exists.
secondary.why: Remix 01 is a modified version with different hack-and-slash gameplay.

all_releases.fidelity: Original social Flash route, now shut down.
all_releases.reason: skip: retired online route; use standalone offline build for preservation.

all_releases.fidelity: Social Flash route, now shut down.

entries.title: Dragon Age: Inquisition
entries.definitive_edition: Game of the Year Edition on Windows

primary.why: Inquisition released on Windows, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, and Xbox One. The Game of the Year Edition bundles the base game and all post-launch content, and later DLC support moved beyond PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. Windows GOTY is therefore both the fidelity and complete-content route.
